description: The curated verification corpus of tools/LintMark.Verify, read by fetch-corpus.ps1. Diversity over quantity: spec and conformance examples, adversarial Markdown tool fixtures, small real-world samples and the DEMA repositories.

fields.name: Unique source name; the folder .corpus/<category>/<name>/ receives the produced files.
fields.repo: GitHub owner/name (members: each member names its own repo).
fields.ref: The default branch of the repository, checked when the manifest was written. The resolved commit SHA is written to .corpus/<category>/<name>/SOURCE.txt, never here.
fields.paths: Repository paths that are considered: a prefix that ends with '/' or one exact file. Only the files picked from them are downloaded.
fields.keepFiles: true: whole files are kept (default for extractor 'none'). Files that are not named *.md get '.md' appended so the verifier finds them.
fields.include: Regex (on the repository-relative path, forward slashes) that selects the whole files; default: \.(md|markdown)$.
fields.exclude: Array of regexes; files that match any are never used.
fields.cap: Largest number of whole files per repository, picked deterministically (sorted, evenly spread). Absent: no cap.
fields.extractor: none | commonmark-examples | markdig-examples | fixture-dots | pandoc-cmd (see fetch-corpus.ps1). The first two read the spec example fence format; fixture-dots reads the title/input/output blocks separated by '.' lines; pandoc-cmd reads the markdown stdin of Pandoc cram tests.
fields.extractFrom: Regex that selects the files given to the extractor.
fields.exampleCap: Largest number of extracted examples per repository, picked deterministically. Absent: no cap.
fields.dedupeAgainst: Names of sources whose extracted examples are not extracted again (exact content match); they must come earlier in this file.
fields.members: An aggregate source: every member names a repo (plus the fields above that it overrides); output goes to files/<owner>__<repo>/ and examples/<owner>__<repo>/.
fields.local: dema only: a folder that is verified in place with the verifier's --dema option and never fetched.

sources.name: commonmark-spec
sources.notes: The CommonMark specification: every example (about 650) as its own file; the tab arrow is converted to a real tab.

sources.name: gfm-spec
sources.notes: The GitHub Flavored Markdown spec and the cmark-gfm extension tests (tables, strikethrough, task lists, autolinks, regressions). Examples that are also in the CommonMark spec are not repeated.

sources.name: markdig-spec
sources.notes: Markdig's extension specs (pipe and grid tables, footnotes, definition lists, abbreviations, attributes, math, emoji, ...): the whole spec files and their examples.

sources.name: pandoc-testsuite
sources.notes: Pandoc's Markdown test documents and its manual, which uses every Pandoc extension.

sources.name: pandoc-cmd
sources.notes: Pandoc's command tests (cram format): the Markdown that is given on standard input to a Markdown reader (markdown, commonmark, gfm and their variants).

sources.name: markdownlint
sources.notes: markdownlint's rule fixtures: deliberately badly formatted Markdown.

sources.name: prettier
sources.notes: Prettier's Markdown formatting inputs (lists, code, tables, CJK, liquid, wiki links, front matter, math, JSX); snapshots are not used.

sources.name: mdformat
sources.notes: mdformat's own style tests and its plugins' fixtures (tables, footnotes, MyST, definition lists): the input of each title/input/output block.

sources.name: remark
sources.notes: The remark family's fixtures. remark itself keeps them in the mdast-util-from-markdown, remark-gfm and remark-frontmatter repositories (the remark repository holds none); only inputs are used.

sources.name: markdown-it
sources.notes: markdown-it's extra fixtures (linkify, typographer, tables, strikethrough, XSS, normalization) and the fixtures of its Python port and plugins (admonitions, containers, footnotes, math, attributes, ...): the input of each block.

sources.name: rumdl
sources.notes: rumdl's test fixtures and its documentation (flavors: MkDocs, MDX, Quarto).

sources.name: awesome-lists
sources.notes: Link-heavy and table-heavy awesome lists.

sources.name: cjk-docs
sources.notes: Chinese and Japanese translations of the Vue documentation: CJK text, full-width punctuation, custom containers.

sources.name: mkdocs-material
sources.notes: MkDocs Material documentation: admonitions, content tabs, attribute lists, abbreviations, footnotes.

sources.name: docusaurus
sources.notes: Docusaurus: the Markdown (not MDX) files of its packages and website, many of them fixtures with front matter, admonitions and headings with ids.

sources.name: jekyll
sources.notes: Jekyll documentation and posts: front matter, Liquid tags, highlight blocks.

sources.name: rust-book
sources.notes: The Rust Book (mdBook): long prose, many fenced code blocks, includes.

sources.name: semantic-line-breaks
sources.notes: Prose with semantic line breaks (one sentence or clause per line): the rustc developer guide uses them, as does the site of the sembr specification.

sources.name: readmes
sources.notes: README.md files of popular projects across ecosystems (JavaScript, Python, Rust, Go, .NET, Ruby, C++, shell), plus a few Home Assistant developer pages.

sources.name: github-docs
sources.notes: A sample of GitHub Docs: Liquid tags, variables and conditionals, reusables, tables, alerts.

sources.name: dema
sources.notes: Every Git repository of DEMA Consulting under the local root, verified in place by the verifier's --dema option (read-only); never fetched.
